answer: Per-identity jitter challenge. On admission, each identity must emit its first 20 requests on a secret schedule with independent random delays; the verifier measures cross-identity timing correlation, using that signal to reject synchronized clusters. Each identity must run as a separate timing island with its own scheduler and clock source. A burst that starts like a falcon (all first requests in one 50 ms window) is denied. Attacker cost: one distinct wall-clock wait schedule and live endpoint per identity, not one shared bot.
